p.i: Siligo, hordeum, Zea, far, oryza, avena, milium, ocymum, panicum, sesamum.

main_text.p: Triticū.Triticum alendis hominibus accommodatissi-mum est, interq; fruges primam semper obtinuit autoritatem: Plurima eius notantur genera, Africum, Thracium, Assyrium, Ægyptium, Italicum, Gallicum, Germanicum, &c Non aliunde quàm à terris fortita nomina, colore tamen, specie, magnitudine & proprietate differentia.

Notæ o-ptimi& laudati tritici.Optimum probumq; triticum est ponderosum, denfum, tota substantia adeo compacta, ut dentib. vix teri diuidiq; queat: quod item plus farinæ reddit, quod aquâ maceratum vel etiam præcoctum ocyus intumescit, ( hoc enim modo agricolationis NB.naturaq; rerum peritî cerealia femina probare solent, probitatisq; vel improbitatis indubitatum id habent experimentum.) Dentib. verò facilè cedens facileq;, frangibile, fractumq;, sirarum & laxum cernitur, magna mole & quantitate exiguum præbet alimentum. Non enim superficies tantum externa consideranda est, sed frangi debet & diuidi. Ut enim venire solet, ut quod extra flauum ac denfum sit, pinsitum postea fractumq; rarum, leve, intus, album appáreat. page.notes: The page is a single text column. The left margin holds three notes: "Triticū." beside the first paragraph; "Notæ optimi & laudati tritici." (hyphenated over four lines) with "NB." beside the middle of the paragraph; and "Triticū falubre & infalubre." (hyphenated over four lines) beside the lower part. The final word "tra-" stands at the lower right and is treated as the catchword. Italic passages are the printed lists of grain names and the Latin "&c". Some words at the scan edge are uncertain and were read from context; "sirarum" and "lolio" are doubtful and may be misprints for "firarum" and "lolio", and "fuperfi.ies" is copied as "superficies". Parts of the lower right are faint, so some words may need checking against the original.
